title: AI Adoption Communications and Role-Based Enablement

questions.question: Why should AI adoption communication be role-specific?
options: Different roles experience different workflow changes
questions.explanation: Each role needs to know what changes, what remains human, and how to practice safely.

questions.question: Which control helps managers support local adoption?
questions.explanation: A manager brief gives leaders talking points, concerns, and escalation triggers.

questions.question: What does a practice task add to an AI rollout?
options: A way to turn communication into behavior
questions.explanation: Practice tasks help people learn the new behavior in a concrete workflow.

questions.question: What should happen when the message gap is high?
options: Clarify the role narrative before scaling
questions.explanation: A message gap means the audience does not yet understand the change.

questions.question: Which rollout needs a full enablement plan?
options: High role impact with resistance signals and manager dependency
questions.explanation: High role impact and friction require structured communication and enablement.

questions.question: Why is a feedback channel part of adoption communication?
options: It makes questions, risks, and adoption blockers visible
It removes the need for managers
questions.explanation: Feedback channels keep concerns and adoption blockers visible after launch.
